prompt:
Below is a policy summary from a UK general election manifesto. Identify the party that produced it. You must choose one.

<text>
Reform UK Manifesto 2024 – Summary (policy proposals and costings only)

Core pledges
- Freeze non-essential immigration; stop small boats via returns to France and ECHR exit; secure detention and rapid (incl. offshore) processing.
- Eliminate NHS waiting lists while remaining free at point of use.
- Raise the income tax threshold to £20,000; higher rate from £70,000.
- Reduce energy bills by scrapping Net Zero policies and related levies; expand domestic oil and gas.

Immigration
- Freeze non-essential immigration; essential health/care skills exempt.
- New Department of Immigration; no UK resettlement for illegal arrivals; pick up and return small boats to France; leave ECHR.
- Detain all illegal arrivals; bar asylum/citizenship if arriving from safe countries; no legal aid for non-citizens; rapid removals.
- Immediate deportation of foreign criminals post-sentence; potential citizenship withdrawal for serious crimes.
- Bar student dependants; restrict post-study stay to essential skills; close abuse schemes.
- Five-year residency and employment to access benefits; tackle health tourism.
- Employer immigration tax: NI 20% on foreign workers (exempt health/care; firms ≤5 staff).
- Indicative figures: savings £5–10bn p.a.; employer immigration tax £4bn p.a.

Slash government waste
- Stop paying interest on QE reserves to commercial banks (claimed saving c. £35bn p.a.).
- 5% efficiency saving across departments without cutting frontline (c. £50bn p.a.).
- Cut foreign aid by 50% (c. £6bn p.a.); strengthen HMRC tax collection.
- Remove retained EU law and reduce regulation.
- Total potential savings cited: c. £91bn p.a.

Economy – personal
- Income tax threshold £20,000; higher rate from £70,000.
- Cut fuel duty by 20p/litre; scrap VAT on energy and environmental levies.
- Stamp duty: 0% to £750k; 2% £750k–£1.5m; 4% over £1.5m.
- Reinstate VAT-free tourist shopping.
- Inheritance tax: 0% under £2m; 20% above (charity option).
- Cost: £70bn p.a.

Economy – business
- No corporation tax on profits up to £100k; main rate 25%→20% (then 15% by year 3).
- Abolish IR35; raise VAT threshold to £150k.
- Abolish business rates for high-street SMEs; 4% online delivery tax on large multinationals; entrepreneurs’ tax to 5%.
- Planning reform; deregulation incl. employment law; tax code simplification.
- Cost: £18bn p.a.

NHS
- Zero basic-rate income tax for NHS/social care staff for 3 years; end training caps; loan write-offs tied to service.
- Use independent and overseas capacity; 20% tax relief on private healthcare/insurance.
- Voucher guarantees: GP 3 days; consultant 3 weeks; operation 9 weeks.
- Efficiency and A&E demand measures; public inquiry into excess deaths.
- Cost: £17bn p.a.

Energy/Net Zero
- Scrap Net Zero and renewable subsidies; fast-track North Sea and shale gas; expand nuclear SMRs.
- Claimed savings: £30bn p.a.

Policing and justice
- Recruit 40,000 officers; zero-tolerance focus; increase stop and search; tougher drug and knife crime penalties; reduce DEI roles.
- Justice: automatic life for violent repeat offenders; budget £10bn→£12bn; reopen magistrates’ courts; 10,000 new detention places; changes to hate crime definition.
- Costs: Policing £3bn p.a.; Justice £2bn p.a.

Education
- Curriculum changes; restrictions on gender-related practices in schools; single-sex facilities.
- 20% tax relief on independent education; no VAT on fees.
- Scrap interest on student loans; cap undergrad numbers; minimum entry standards; expand PRUs; optional 2-year degrees.
- Cost: £5bn p.a.

Benefits
- Incentives to work via higher tax threshold; training/apprenticeship support.
- Two-strike rule on job offers; face-to-face assessments (exempt severe cases).
- Savings: £15bn p.a.

Brexit
- Repeal retained EU law; abandon Windsor Framework; prepare TCA renegotiation; avoid EU defence integration.

Defence
- Spend 2.5% of GDP by year 3, 3% within 6 years; pay uplift; legal protections; new Veterans department; recruit 30,000; procurement reform.
- Cost: £14bn p.a.

Housing
- Fast-track brownfield; prioritise locals in social housing; restore landlord mortgage interest deductibility; drop Renters’ Reform Bill; leasehold protections.
- Cost: neutral.

Children and families
- 25% transferable marriage allowance (as finances allow); front-load child benefit (ages 1–4); single-sex spaces; measures on child online harms.
- Cost: £8bn p.a.

Transport and infrastructure
- Scrap remaining HS2 (save £25bn one-off); ban ULEZ/LTNs; review 20mph zones; regional upgrades.
- Utilities: 50% public/50% UK pension fund ownership model; cap standing charges; merge infrastructure bodies.
- Savings: £25bn one-off; £5bn p.a.

Agriculture and fisheries
- Farming budget to £3bn; replace climate-linked subsidies; reduce red tape; buy-British targets.
- Fisheries: license/limit foreign access; ban supertrawlers; expand patrols; rebuild processing.
- Costs: Agriculture £2bn p.a.; Fisheries £2bn p.a.

Pensions and social care
- Royal Commission on social care; address offshore tax practices in care; pension system review; implement Mineworkers Pension recommendations.

Constitutional and governance
- Leave ECHR; reform House of Lords and civil service leadership; restrict postal voting; PR referendum; British Bill of Rights.

Other governance
- Review WHO engagement and CBDC; replace Equalities Act/DEI rules; Free Speech Bill; reform BBC incl. scrapping licence fee; new anti-corruption unit.

Funding summary (party’s figures)
- Savings: £150bn p.a. + £10bn p.a. from assumed extra growth = £160bn p.a.
- Costs: £141bn p.a.
</text>

Respond with a single JSON object and nothing else, with these keys in this order:

{
  "evidence": "<what in the text informed your choice>",
  "confidence": "high" | "medium" | "low",
  "party": one of ['Labour', 'Conservative', 'Reform UK', 'Liberal Democrats', 'Green Party']
}
